claims.text: The initial and baseline material is a W-20Cu (wt.%) metal-matrix composite.
The intervention adds 10 wt.% Ti, 5 wt.% Zr, and 5 wt.% Hf to produce a W-20Cu-10Ti-5Zr-5Hf composite.
The modified composition constitutes a high-entropy-alloy composition change.
Adding Ti, Zr, and Hf will form a homogeneous nanoscale dispersion of HEA phases within the W-Cu matrix.
The composition change will increase the phonon mean free path.
The composition change will reduce phonon scattering.
Increasing phonon mean free path and reducing phonon scattering will enhance thermal conductivity.
A stable nanoscale dispersion of HEA phases will retain mechanical durability.
A stable nanoscale dispersion of HEA phases will retain irradiation resistance.
The modified composite will retain mechanical durability under temperatures up to 1000°C and irradiation doses up to 10 dpa.
The modified composite will retain irradiation resistance under temperatures up to 1000°C and irradiation doses up to 10 dpa.
The baseline W-20Cu composite has a thermal conductivity of 120 W/m-K under the comparison conditions.
The intervention will raise thermal conductivity from 120 W/m-K to 138 W/m-K.
The predicted conductivity increase relative to an otherwise comparable W-20Cu composite is 15%.
Temperatures up to 1000°C and irradiation doses up to 10 dpa represent high-temperature, high-radiation fusion-reactor conditions.
The actual conductivity increase may depend on processing conditions and microstructural evolution.
A measured post-exposure thermal conductivity below 125 W/m-K will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis specifically predicts 138 W/m-K, but it is falsified only below 125 W/m-K. Thus results from 125 to below 138 W/m-K would fail the stated quantitative prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.

The phrase 'adding' 20 wt.% total Ti, Zr, and Hf to an existing W-20Cu composition is inconsistent or ambiguous with the final notation W-20Cu-10Ti-5Zr-5Hf, which implies a final 60 wt.% W balance rather than simple addition to the original composite.
